away and flat-bats it towards mid off. Henry seems to call Sodhi through for the single 
and the latter makes a half-hearted attempt to get to the other end. That gives Shadab

Will Young: (On not getting the hundred) Cricket is a funny game, you always want a few 
more. As an opening batter, your job is to set the platform and I think I did that. I think 
the surface is quite low and slow. Against the seamers, I tried to hit straight. Against the 
spinners, there were a few more gaps so I tried to manipulate it. I reckon it (the score) is 
about par. At the start of the innings, we would have taken 280. Chapman played really 
well and at that point, we thought 320 was on the cards. We will take 300 (299). I will 
take some learnings from playing against such a high-quality attack. 
Pakistan, meanwhile, will be pleased with how their bowlers responded to pressure 
situations. Babar kept persisting with his spinners in the final ten overs, and Usama 
responded with the wicket of Latham. Earlier, Shadab had accounted for Chapman and 
Young, with the leg-spinners combining for four wickets in total. Before a ball had been 
bowled today, Pakistan might have wanted to keep New Zealand down to a score below 
280. But after the start the visitors got, they would be happy chasing 300, although they 
will have to bat well to ace this run-chase. Rvel will be here to take you through the 
second innings! 
7:15pm An excellent finish to the innings for Pakistan. They only gave away 36 in the 
last five overs and also picked up five wickets, with Rauf and Shaheen doing their bit at 
the end. Prior to that, though, New Zealand had set themselves up for a strong finish, 
courtesy of Young and Latham's half-centuries. Chapman was also belligerent during 
his 33-ball stay at the crease, with McConchie also popping up with a 25-ball 26. The 
problem for the Kiwis, though, was that none of their middle order batters batted deep 
into the innings and ensured that they finished with a flourish.
